# rbtree-lab: project rules
## Commands
- Build & unit tests: ‘make test‘
- Sanitizers: ‘make asan‘ Valgrind: ‘make memcheck‘
- A change is DONE only when all three pass. Always run them; show output.
- Route all allocations in src/rbtree.c through two rb_malloc and rb_free found in src/rb_alloc.c.
## Hard constraints
- NEVER modify include/rbtree.h. It is the graded contract.
- Use include/rbtree.h as a strict reference for allocations and ownership such; every function must follow the rules outlined there.
- Check every allocation. malloc can return NULL; a NULL return must
leave the tree unchanged and return the documented error code.
- NEVER weaken, skip, or delete a test to make the suite pass. If a test
looks wrong, stop and explain why instead.
- 'rb_insert' must 'rb_malloc + memcpy' its own copy 'k'; it must never store 'key' itself or free it
## Style
- C23. -Wall -Wextra -Werror must stay clean. No VLAs.
- Error handling: goto-cleanup pattern for multi-allocation functions.
- Prefer the smallest diff that passes. Do not refactor unrelated code.
- Every non-obvious loop gets a one-line invariant comment.
## Workflow
- For any multi-file or algorithmic change: propose a plan and wait for
approval before editing.
- Never commit to the git repository.
- [rb_validate must check root-black](feedback_rb_validate_root_black.md) — required invariant even though header comment omits it

# Plan: table-driven `rb_delete` fixup tests

## Context

`tests/test_rbtree.c`'s `test_bst_delete` (lines 989-1287) was written before deletion
fixup existed. Its cases 4-8 pin exact BST-splice pointers using all-black `mk_node`
fixtures, but several of those fixtures actually do have `removedColor == RB_BLACK`
and so already run the fixup loop today (e.g. case 7/8's two-children deletes) —
the tests just never noticed, because they never call `rb_validate()` after deleting
and never assert on post-delete colors. That's the gap: now that fixup is implemented,
we need cases that deliberately exercise the fixup *cases* (red sibling → rotation,
propagate-up recoloring, successor promotion feeding into fixup, and deleting the
root itself) and check the result with `rb_validate()`, not just raw pointers.

This only touches `tests/test_rbtree.c` (test-only, no `src/` change, no algorithm
design) — per CLAUDE.md this doesn't strictly require the "multi-file/algorithmic"
plan-approval gate, but since we're already in plan mode, here's the concrete table.

## Fixture technique

Same as the existing suite: build trees directly with `mk_node` (bypassing
`rb_insert`/insert-fixup) so every case's pre-delete shape and colors are pinned
exactly, matching `test_bst_delete` cases 4-8 and `test_rb_validate`'s style.
`rb_create(NULL)` (no `value_free`) since `mk_node` leaves `value = NULL`.

## New table: `delete_fixup_cases`

Add after `test_bst_delete`, a new `test_rb_delete_fixup(void)` function driven by a
table of function-pointer cases (mirrors `create_cases`/`insert_cases`'s table style,
extended with build/verify function pointers since each fixup case needs a
differently-shaped fixture):

```c
typedef struct {
    const char *name;
    rbtree_t *(*build)(void);   /* pinned pre-delete fixture; asserts rb_validate==0 */
    const char *key;            /* key to delete */
    size_t expect_size_after;
    void (*verify)(rbtree_t *t); /* case-specific structural/color asserts */
} delete_fixup_case_t;
```

A common driver `run_delete_fixup_case(const delete_fixup_case_t *c)`:
1. `t = c->build()`
2. `assert(rb_validate(t) == 0)` — sanity-check the fixture itself is a legal RB tree
   *before* deleting (so a failure clearly points at the fixture, not `rb_delete`)
3. `fault_malloc_arm(0); rc = rb_delete(t, c->key); free_count == 2; fault_malloc_disarm();`
4. `assert(rc == 0); assert(rb_size(t) == c->expect_size_after);`
5. `assert(rb_find(t, c->key) == NULL);`
6. `assert(rb_validate(t) == 0)` — the invariant the old suite never checked post-delete
7. `rb_foreach` into a `collect_ctx_t`, assert count matches and keys are strictly
   ascending (same pattern as case 9's end-to-end check)
8. `c->verify(t)` — case-specific pointer/color assertions
9. `destroy_and_check_frees(t, node_count)` (node_count is `expect_size_after + 1`,
   the one node freed by delete plus the survivors)

## The four required cases (minimum)

**1. `delete_red_leaf`** — deleting a red leaf takes `removedColor == RB_RED`, so the
fixup `while` loop never runs at all.
Fixture: root `"m"`(B), left `"d"`(R, leaf), right `"t"`(B, leaf). Delete `"d"`.
`verify`: `root->left == t->nil`, root itself unchanged (`"m"`, still B), `root->right`
still the original `"t"` node/color.

**2. `delete_black_leaf_red_sibling`** — the flagship red-sibling case (fixup Case 1
rotation into Case 2 recolor), fully hand-traced so every post-delete pointer/color is
pinned:
Fixture: root `"m"`(B) / target `"f"`(B, leaf) / sibling `"t"`(R) with `"t"`'s two
children `"p"`(B, leaf) and `"x"`(B, leaf). Delete `"f"`.
Trace: `fixNode = nil` after splicing `"f"` out; sibling `"t"` is RED → Case 1:
`t`→BLACK, `m`→RED, `rotate_left(m)`. New sibling is `"p"` (BLACK, both children nil)
→ Case 2: `p`→RED, `fixNode` climbs to `m`, loop exits (`m` is RED), final
`fixNode->color = BLACK` recolors `m` BLACK (no-op, already was after Case1... note
Case1 set `m` RED, so this final step actually turns it back BLACK).
`verify`: new `t->root == <old "t" node>`, color BLACK; `root->left == <old "m" node>`,
color BLACK; `root->right == <old "x" node>`, unchanged BLACK; `<old "m">->left ==
t->nil`; `<old "m">->right == <old "p" node>`, color RED.

**3. `delete_two_children_black_successor`** — a non-root node with two children whose
in-order successor is BLACK, so removing it feeds a real node into the fixup loop
(not just a boundary case). Fixture: root `"m"`(B), left `"d"`(B) [target] with
`"d"`'s children `"b"`(R, leaf) and `"f"`(B, leaf) [successor — `"f"` has no left
child, so `rb_inorder_successor` returns it directly], right `"t"`(B, leaf). Delete
`"d"`.
`verify`: kept light on deep colors (derived by the fixup loop, not hand-traced) —
assert `root->left == <old "f" node>` (successor promoted into `"d"`'s slot),
`<old "f">->left == <old "b" node>` and its parent pointer fixed up, `<old "f">->color
== BLACK` (successor always takes the deleted node's color). Correctness of any
resulting recoloring is covered by step 6's `rb_validate` check, not asserted by hand.

**4. `delete_root_two_children`** — deleting the root itself when it has two children,
so the successor gets promoted all the way into `t->root`. Fixture: root `"m"`(B)
[target], left `"d"`(B, leaf), right `"t"`(B) with `"t"`'s children `"p"`(B, leaf)
[successor] and `"x"`(B, leaf). Delete `"m"`.
`verify`: `t->root == <old "p" node>`, color BLACK (successor always inherits the
deleted node's color, and the root must stay BLACK per the invariant this repo's
memory already flags — see `rb_validate`'s root-black check); `t->root->left == <old
"d" node>`; `t->root->right == <old "t" node>`; `<old "t">->left == t->nil` (successor
spliced out of its old spot). Fine-grained recoloring left to `rb_validate` again.

## Wiring

- Add `test_rb_delete_fixup();` to `main()` after `test_bst_delete();`.
- No changes to `include/rbtree.h` or `src/rbtree.c`.

## Verification

Run the `battery` skill (`make test`, `make asan`, `make memcheck`, with `make clean`
between asan/memcheck per this repo's known quirk) and show output; all three must
pass for the change to be DONE per CLAUDE.md.

All three pass clean: `make test`, `make asan`, and `make memcheck` (with the `make clean` between them this repo needs). Added `test_rb_delete_fixup` in [tests/test_rbtree.c](tests/test_rbtree.c#L1288), a table-driven suite of 4 cases exercising `rb_delete`'s fixup loop:

- **`delete_black_leaf_red_sibling`** — Case 1 rotation into Case 2 recolor, fully pointer/color-traced

- **`delete_root_two_children`** — deleting the root itself, successor promoted all the way into `t->root`

Each case builds a `mk_node`-pinned fixture (asserted valid via `rb_validate` before deleting), then the shared driver checks the delete return code, free count, size, absence of the deleted key, `rb_validate` post-delete, ascending in-order traversal, and case-specific structural/color assertions — closing the gap where the old `test_bst_delete` never checked `rb_validate` after a delete.
